final_rationale: The verdict remains noncompliant. The Actor response introduced no new admissible evidence and instead narrowed the claim to a caveated certification position based on the same record already audited. That reframing is useful but not sufficient. Under the policy text, rollout controls and monitoring can mitigate a material model-card weakness only if they exclude the affected use case or include reviewed risk acceptance explaining why exposure is acceptable. The admissible record, including the Actor's concessions, still shows that the affected public benefits eligibility segment remains in scope, the county gate does not exclude it, and the available risk-acceptance draft is incomplete. Because the unresolved compliance predicate remains unmet, this is not merely a disclosure-quality issue and cannot be upgraded to compliant_with_caveats on the current evidence.
remaining_concerns: The affected public benefits eligibility segment remains exposed in the initial rollout.
The county-based rollout gate does not exclude the affected segment.
The available risk-acceptance draft is incomplete, so reviewed risk acceptance covering the exposed segment is not established.
The stated policy requires either exclusion of the affected use case or reviewed risk acceptance; the record shows neither predicate is satisfied.
Rollback, monitoring, and a 7% initial rollout do not satisfy the policy condition while the affected segment remains exposed.
A caveated certification record and added disclosure may improve accuracy of the packet, but they do not convert the present record into compliance under the stated policy.
